flags.name: Flag 1 - CF Dashboard
flags.description: In the Cloudflare console, navigate to Zero Trust from the left-hand menu. Navigate to Insights and Logs from the new left-hand menu and select Dashboards from the dropdown. Open the Access dashboard, set the event window to 30 days, and review the Access Events by Type panel. The Cloudflare dashboards provide a catalog of saved analytics views for reporting and investigation. Analytics Dashboards provide visualizations of your log data. The Access event analytics dashboard lets users review login attempts to the applications they protected behind Access. Set the event window to 30 days. Pay attention to Access events by type. What is the least common type? The flag is the type of access event.

hints.description: Two of the four types are the obvious pair; you want one of remaining two.
Three letters. It is the handoff to your IdP.
The flag is <s1-answer>SSO</s1-answer>.

flags.name: Flag 2 - CF Dashboard
flags.description: In the Cloudflare console, navigate to Zero Trust from the left-hand menu. Navigate to Insights and Logs from the new left-hand menu and select Dashboards from the dropdown. Open the DNS query analytics dashboard, set the event window to 30 days, and review the Gateway insights for DNS queries section. The Cloudflare dashboards provide a catalog of saved analytics views for reporting and investigation. Analytics Dashboards provide visualizations of your log data. The DNS query analytics dashboard lets users review queries handled by Gateway based on their DNS policies. Set the event window to 30 days. Pay attention to the Gateway insights for DNS queries section. The flag is the number of DNS actions allowed by rule.

hints.description: The flag is displayed under the DNS Action subsection.
The flag is <s1-answer>1420</s1-answer>.

flags.name: Flag 3 - CF Investigation
flags.description: In the Cloudflare console, select the soledrop.co domain, open the Security dropdown from the left-hand menu, and choose Web Assets. From the nav bar at the top, select the Upgrade tab and review the discovered endpoints panel. The API Shield preview tells users what endpoints need protecting, and can offer valuable analytics to help with incident prevention. What is the endpoint destination for the top discovered endpoints? The flag is the endpoint destination.

hints.description: The flag is in the Endpoint column of the specified section.
It is the API path the status page polls for the live incident state.
The flag is <s1-answer>/api/incident</s1-answer>.

flags.name: Flag 4 - CF Investigation
flags.token: Likely account takeover attacks detected in login requests
flags.description: In the Cloudflare console, select the soledrop.co domain, open the Security dropdown from the left-hand menu, and choose Analytics. Scroll to the Suspicious Activity panel and read the top finding. What does the top Suspicious Activity finding say is happening? The flag is the name of the activity.
flags.plainAnswer: Likely account takeover attacks detected in login requests

hints.description: Read the headline of the top finding, not the request counts beside it.
It is about likely malicious activity related to user accounts.
The flag is <s1-answer>Likely account takeover attacks detected in login requests</s1-answer>.

flags.name: Flag 5 - Oneflare Custom Dashboad
flags.description: In the SentinelOne console, navigate to Dashboards from the left-hand menu and open the OneFlare 'Cloudflare Threat Detection' custom dashboard. Find the Attack Types panel and read its title/description. Custom dashboards are helpful because they allow analysts to display the information they think is most relevant. Dashboards allow this information to be readily accessible for threat analysis. The Attack Types panel filters on a WAF ML attack score at or below a threshold. What is that threshold? The flag is the number of WAF blocks that have occurred.

hints.description: The flag is found in the description of the <s1-label>Web Application Firewall (WAF)</s1-label> subsection.
Remember low = malicious. The band is 1 to this number.
The flag is <s1-answer>20</s1-answer>.

flags.name: Flag 6 - CF WAF Rule
flags.description: In the Cloudflare console, select the soledrop.co domain, open the Security dropdown from the left-hand menu, and choose Security Rules. Read down the Action column. One rule on this zone deliberately does not block — it only records matches so the SOC can see them. What action is it set to? The flag is the action.

hints.description: Read the <s1-label>Action</s1-label> column top to bottom; one value is not an enforcement action at all.
It produces evidence without changing what the visitor experiences.
The flag is <s1-answer>Log</s1-answer>.

flags.name: Flag 7 - Oneflare Custom Dashboard
flags.description:
<s1-nav>Navigate to Dashboards on the SentinelOne console. Select Custom dashboards, then the Cloudflare dashboard. Set lookback window to 72 hours.</s1-nav>
<s1-flag-body>
According to the custom Oneflare dashboard, how many HTTP requests have we recieved within the last 72 hours
</s1-flag-body>
<s1-flag example="4000">The flag is the number of HTTPS requests recieved within the last 72 hours.</s1-flag>

hints.description: *Screenshot of where to look*
The flag is 6440.

flags.name: Flag 8 - HTTP Traffic
flags.description:
<s1-nav>On the left hand side navigate to Analytics. Select HTTP Traffic from the dropdown. Set the event window to 30 days.</s1-nav>
<s1-flag-body>
In HTTP Traffic, how many HTTP requests are going through CF?</s1-flag-body>
<s1-flag example="100,000">The flag is the total number of HTTP requests</s1-flag>

hints.description: The flag is <s1-answer>300,000</s1-answer>.

flags.name: Flag 9 - DNS Tunneling
flags.description:
<s1-nav>Find the Alerts view from the menu on the left.</s1-nav>
<s1-flag-body>
From the Alerts view, locate the Alert cluster that has CF-Gateway-DNSTunnel — DNS Tunneling / C2 Beaconing (Gateway DNS) in the Alert name column.
</s1-flag-body>
<s1-flag example="30">The flag is the number of alerts in this cluster.</s1-flag>

hints.description: The flag is 55

flags.name: Flag 10 - DNS Tunneling
flags.description:
<s1-nav>Find the Alerts view from the menu on the left. 
From the Alerts view, locate the Alert cluster that has CF-Gateway-DNSTunnel — DNS Tunneling / C2 Beaconing (Gateway DNS) in the Alert name column. Click on any one of these alerts</s1-nav>

<s1-flag-body>
The Purple AI Alert description will be in the popup on the right hand side.
</s1-flag-body>
<s1-flag example="">The flag is what Purple AI says repeated long TXT queries are indicative of.</s1-flag>

hints.description: The flag is <s1-answer>base32-encoded data exfiltration</s1-answer>.

flags.name: Flag 11 - DNS Tunneling
flags.description:
<s1-nav>Find the Alerts view from the menu on the left. 
From the Alerts view, locate the Alert cluster that has CF-Gateway-DNSTunnel — DNS Tunneling / C2 Beaconing (Gateway DNS) in the Alert name column. Click on any one of these alerts.</s1-nav>
<s1-flag-body>
Use the Purple AI Alert Description to find the MITRE ATT&CK reference associated with Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol.
</s1-flag-body>
<s1-flag example="T####">The flag is the MITRE ATT&CK ID</s1-flag>

hints.description:
Read through the Purple AI Alert Description.

Find the MITRE ATT&CK ID that comes right before (Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol).

The code follows the following format: T####.
The flag is <s1-answer>T1048</s1-answer>.

flags.name: Flag 12 - Mitigate
flags.description:
<s1-nav>Find the Alerts view from the menu on the left. 
From the Alerts view, locate the Alert cluster that has CF-Gateway-DNSTunnel — DNS Tunneling / C2 Beaconing (Gateway DNS) in the Alert name column. Click on any one of these alerts.</s1-nav>
<s1-flag-body>
Find the Actions button towards the top right of the alert. Click on the Actions button and proceed to mark the alert as a threat.
</s1-flag-body>
<s1-flag example="">The flag is the pair of threat policy options we have available to us.</s1-flag>

hints.description: The flag is <s1-answer>Suspicious / Malicious</s1-answer>
